# Leaflet

Small open-source JavaScript map library — tile layers, markers, polylines, layer toggles, and very
little else. It appears twice in this corpus, in two different repositories, **at the same version
(1.9.4) from the same CDN**, which is itself a finding about how this developer reaches for a map.

## `Optimization Methods` — the route explorer

`instance_generator/map_app/city.template.html` loads Leaflet from unpkg:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css" />
<script  src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js"></script>
```

Python generates one HTML page per city from that template with the route geometry baked in as
coordinate arrays. Each solver gets its own toggleable layer — `greedy`, `blind_ga`, `lbbs` and the
tuned variants — so a reader can flip between plans on the same map instead of comparing two static
PNGs. There are per-depot layers and a Drive/Evolve animation for watching a solution form.

This is the presentation half of [[multi-depot-vehicle-routing]], and it is why the repo needed a
`.gitattributes` marking `output/**` as `linguist-generated`: the baked-in coordinate arrays are
megabytes of generated `.js` that would otherwise make GitHub call [[optimization-methods]] a
JavaScript project.

## `Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories` — Q-HYDRO Wrocław

The Q-HYDRO app in `lab5_GraphTheory` maps a 25-node Lower-Silesian gravimeter mesh, also on Leaflet
1.9.4 from a CDN, with map tiles and IBM Plex fonts likewise remote. It sits beside a second lab-5 app
(SentinelNet) that vendors [[react]] and has **zero external URLs** — two apps, one directory, exactly
opposite dependency policies. See [[graph-connectivity-and-resilience]].

## The consistent exception to a consistent rule

Both repos otherwise take vendoring seriously. `Optimization Methods` ships a standard-library-only
C++ solver and a study guide with three plain `<script>` tags and no build step
([[zero-dependency-no-build-step]]); `Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories` went to the trouble of
precompiling JSX so SentinelNet runs offline.

**Maps are where that rule gets suspended, in both repos independently.** The reason is not written
down anywhere, but it is not mysterious: a map without tiles is not a degraded map, it is a blank
rectangle, so the offline story is already lost at the tile server and vendoring the 42 KB library
buys nothing. Both repos document the CDN dependency as a graceful-degradation case rather than
hiding it, which is the honest version of the compromise —
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]].

The consequence is real, though: neither map app opens usefully from `file://` on a plane, unlike
every other static deliverable in the corpus ([[offline-first-static-deliverable]]).
